prompts.prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Create ONE high-resolution wide triptych of three discrete full-body photorealistic basketball coaching photographs, equal-width panels separated by generous empty space, aspect ratio 3:2. Feature the same 12-year-old boy in burgundy jersey labeled MUSTANGS 23 and navy shorts in each panel. Simple seamless dark navy studio backdrop, no gym, no scenery, no graphic labels or captions. Soft natural studio lighting. Show every shoe and all fingertips with margin. Anatomically correct realistic youth build, two arms, two legs, five fingers per visible hand, no ghost limbs. This will be a step-by-step reference for REBOUND SECURITY. LEFT panel: player rises in a small balanced two-foot jump, arms extended high, catching a single basketball firmly with both hands above forehead; both shoes a little above floor, eyes on ball. CENTER panel: player landed with knees flexed, feet comfortably shoulder width, basketball secured against upper chest under chin, elbows naturally bent close to ribs, NOT flared horizontally. RIGHT panel: same player in balanced quarter-turned stance with feet on floor, ball held tightly with two hands near far hip behind his torso to protect it, eyes up scanning for outlet. Maintain clear hand-ball contact and believable joints. Do not put any arrows, text boxes, watermarks, court, or other people. Reference image is style inspiration only; replace its wide-elbow pose with tucked elbows as described.

Use case: scientific-educational. Create one photorealistic basketball instruction triptych, three equal-width photographic panels in a wide 3:2 image. In EACH panel show two 12-year-old boys full body head-to-shoes: burgundy MUSTANGS 23 jersey defender and blue THUNDER 11 jersey ball handler. Plain seamless dark navy studio, absolutely no gym/scenery/graphic labels/arrows. Anatomically accurate, normal youth proportions, exactly two arms and two legs each, five fingers, visible full shoes and no merged hands. Camera three-quarter side view. Leave clear space between players, approximately one arm length, no touching. LEFT panel: blue attacker holds one ball near right hip in a balanced stance; burgundy defender faces him with knees softly bent, feet a little wider than shoulders, torso balanced, nearest open hand reaching slightly toward the ball with bent elbow and a clear air gap, other hand raised around chest height toward an imaginary passing window, NOT touching chest or shoulder. CENTER panel: blue attacker low right-hand dribble with ball between right hand and floor; burgundy defender shifts laterally in balanced stance, near hand low toward ball without reaching across body, other hand available chest-high, chest staying in front. RIGHT panel: blue player has picked ball up with two hands near chest; burgundy defender remains balanced at safe non-contact distance with both hands raised to obstruct passing windows. Every photo must show both players completely, with no overlapping body parts that obscure their arms. NO hand on opponent. Natural realistic photographic textures. This REPLACES a flawed defensive posture sequence.

Use case: scientific-educational. ONE photorealistic basketball technique triptych, THREE equal-width panels left to right, wide 3:2 image. Plain dark navy seamless studio, no gym or scenery, no labels/arrows. Same 12-year-old boy burgundy MUSTANGS 23 jersey, navy shorts and white/navy basketball shoes in each panel, entire body and shoes visible with margins. Teaching a REVERSE (BACK) PIVOT on his LEFT foot, RIGHT foot moves backward. Fixed camera at front three-quarter view, floor subtly visible. LEFT panel: balanced athletic stance, knees bent, left shoe firmly on floor, both hands hold ball near chest, eyes up. MIDDLE panel: left forefoot stays at its original pivot point; right foot is lifted just off floor and sweeps BACKWARD behind his original hip line, hips and shoulders turn together, back/side of right shoulder rotates toward camera, ball pulled tightly to protected hip with both hands; realistic knees never twisted. RIGHT panel: finishes about a quarter-turn from starting direction, right foot set behind original starting position, left forefoot still on SAME spot, heels can turn, balanced feet shoulder width, ball protected near far hip, head turned up to see floor. Do not show a forward crossover. No ghost limbs or multiple exposures; exactly two arms and two legs in each panel. Prioritize credible footwork and ball grip over dramatic poses.

Use case: scientific-educational. ONE photorealistic basketball technique triptych, THREE equally wide panels left to right, wide 3:2 image. Plain dark navy seamless studio backdrop with subtle floor, no gym, no scenery, no labels or arrows. Same 12-year-old boy wearing burgundy MUSTANGS 23 jersey, navy shorts and white/navy shoes in each frame. Full body including toes and hands, ample margin. Teaching a FRONT (FORWARD) PIVOT on the LEFT foot. RIGHT foot sweeps FORWARD in a controlled quarter-circle, chest turns toward the new direction. Fixed camera three-quarter front view. LEFT panel: both feet comfortably apart, knees flexed, two-hand ball grip by hip, eyes up. MIDDLE panel: left forefoot planted in exactly same floor spot, right foot lifted just above floor and moving FORWARD ahead of original hip line, hips and chest rotate together; basketball held with two hands close to torso during a compact low sweep below an imaginary defender's hands, elbows bent close, no flinging ball. RIGHT panel: right foot set forward at new angle, left pivot foot turned on its ball without sliding to a new spot; player balanced with knees flexed, ball at ready hip, eyes up ready pass or shoot. Anatomically correct youth proportions, no extra fingers, no crossed/twisted legs, no blended poses, no extreme stretches.

Use case: scientific-educational. ONE wide 3:2 photorealistic basketball teaching triptych. THREE equal-width frames, each completely contains two full-body 12-year-old boys with all shoes visible and wide blank margins. Isolated plain dark navy studio, no scenery, no graphics or text except jerseys. Burgundy MUSTANGS 23 is DEFENDER; blue THUNDER 11 is OFFENSE. LEFT: Thunder in shooting-ready stance with ball at chest, Mustang approaching under control then braking with short steps at an arm-length cushion, hips bent, one hand up, no touch. CENTER: Thunder shooting a jump shot with ball just above fingertips and both feet slightly lifted; Mustang stays grounded, upright raised hand contests in his OWN space with visible air gap between defender's fingers and shooter's hand, arm, and face. Clear empty landing space in front of shooter. RIGHT: Separate close-range verticality example, Thunder holds ball overhead ready to finish, Mustang already established in front with BOTH arms straight up over his own shoulders, shoulders hips feet stacked, no body contact, no lean into shooter. Camera side/three-quarter angle makes space between them obvious. Realistic age-appropriate anatomy, exactly two arms/two legs each, no extra fingers/merged hands. Do not show defender swatting, jumping forward, touching shooter or undercutting. No hoop needed; this is body positioning reference.

Use case: scientific-educational. ONE photorealistic basketball technique triptych, three equally wide separate scenes in landscape 3:2 format. Same 12-year-old players; burgundy MUSTANGS 23 is offensive SCREENER, blue THUNDER 11 defender. Plain dark navy studio, no court scenery, no labels arrows or inset captions. Each frame shows both boys completely head to shoes with margins. LEFT: Mustang approaches an empty spot BESIDE Thunder, still a full normal step away and clearly in his sight, balanced posture about to stop, hands tucked near abdomen, not touching. CENTER: Mustang is completely stationary in balanced shoulder-width stance, feet parallel planted, knees softly bent, torso vertical, hands held together close to abdomen, elbows tucked, no ball. Thunder is actively taking a step AROUND the outside of Mustang with clear air gap, not crashing, grappling or leaning, direction can be read from his step. RIGHT: Thunder has cleared the stationary screener and is moving away; Mustang now turns balanced and raises open hands at chest height as a receiving target. Do not introduce a ball or third player. No flared elbows, grabbing, spread legs outside a normal stance, shoulder bumps or abnormal joints. Realistic youth anatomy and five-finger hands. This demonstrates arrive, HOLD, then release only after defender/cutter clears.

Use case: scientific-educational. ONE wide 3:2 photorealistic basketball coaching triptych, THREE equal-width frames with full-body 12-year-old boys. Burgundy MUSTANGS 23 is offense with ball, blue THUNDER 11 passive defender. Plain dark navy studio, no scenery, no annotations. LEFT: Mustang stationary in balanced knees-flexed stance, angled side-on with torso between defender and ball; ball held in TWO hands tightly at the FAR hip, elbows bent close, head up. Thunder is a safe arm length away, no contact. CENTER: Separate LIVE-DRIBBLE example, Mustang using outside hand to push basketball down beside far hip, shoulder and hip between Thunder and ball, hand on top/side not under ball, free forearm bent naturally close to own body NOT pushing opponent. Feet low to floor, preparing to step BACK from pressure. RIGHT: continuation of CENTER: Mustang has taken two short controlled backward steps, still side-on and dribbling on outside of body, now clearly farther away from Thunder; eyes looking up, head toward play, balanced stance with feet not tangled. Show exactly ONE basketball in each frame. Important left is a held-ball example, center/right a different live-dribble example; NO frozen ball under palm, no carrying, no stiff arm or contact. Leave roomy margins; realistic limbs and hands.

Use case: scientific-educational. ONE photorealistic basketball teaching triptych with THREE equally wide frames, landscape 3:2. Single same 12-year-old boy in burgundy MUSTANGS 23 jersey and navy shorts, full body including all shoes/hands in each frame. Plain dark navy seamless studio backdrop, no court, no graphic labels or arrows. Sequence: LEFT player catching a single basketball with both hands while slightly airborne in a short low hop, eyes track ball, both shoes lifted slightly together. CENTER player has landed simultaneously on BOTH feet, shoulder width, knees flexed and hips loaded, ball gathered close to chest with two hands, stable balanced stance and neutral ankles. RIGHT player remains on same two feet in balanced ready stance, ball near shooting hip, head up looking at imaginary teammate, elbows tucked, ready to pass/shoot/start dribble. No exaggerated jump, no squatting too deep, no scattered fingers or extra limbs. This is a simple catch-in-air, simultaneous landing, eyes-up read sequence; realistic youth proportions, soft studio lighting.

Edit this basketball triptych. Preserve the three-panel composition, boy, jersey, plain navy background, and ball grip. Correct the footwork to a controlled low REVERSE PIVOT, NOT a high heel kick. In the MIDDLE panel lower the raised right shoe to within one inch of the floor, knee only softly bent, so it sweeps backward LOW in an arc. Keep left forefoot planted. In the RIGHT panel keep comfortable shoulder-width separation, knees flexed, no twisted knees. In ALL panels keep the player similar scale and whole shoes visible. Chest may turn away as he opens backward. Do not add arrows, labels or text. Anatomy must stay realistic.

Edit this basketball triptych to correct a FORWARD PIVOT. Keep same boy, jersey, navy studio and three panels. The current middle panel kicking forward and final crossed legs are INCORRECT. MIDDLE: lower his raised right shoe to one inch above floor, knee softly bent, sweeping in a SHORT forward quarter-circle near the floor around planted left forefoot. No high kick. Rotate hips and chest together toward camera left. RIGHT: uncross legs and put right shoe down at new quarter-turn angle with clear shoulder-width distance between feet, knees flexed. LEFT foot remains pivot. Ball stays close in two hands, moving in a compact LOW sweep below waist in middle, back to hip in final. Entire player and all shoes visible in each frame, same scale, accurate anatomy, no arrows or labels.
